meaning: Supabase stopped sending auth emails (signup confirmation, magic links, password resets) because the project hit its hourly email limit. The built-in email sender allows only a handful per hour.
causes: You are using Supabase's default SMTP, which is for testing only and has a very low hourly limit.
Repeated testing of signup or magic links from the same project.
A bug calls signUp or signInWithOtp in a loop or on every render.

steps.text: Set up custom SMTP: Authentication > Emails > SMTP Settings (Resend, Postmark, SendGrid, AWS SES all work). This lifts the tiny default limit.
After custom SMTP, adjust limits under Authentication > Rate Limits.
Make sure the email call only runs on a button submit, and disable the button while it's pending.
While testing, confirm users manually in Authentication > Users or use password sign-in so you don't burn the email quota.

prompt: Users see 'email rate limit exceeded' from Supabase. Make sure signUp, signInWithOtp and resetPasswordForEmail only run on explicit form submit with a disabled-while-sending button and a 60-second resend cooldown, and show a friendly 'Too many emails, try again in a few minutes' message for this error. I will configure custom SMTP in Supabase.

faq.a: The limit is per hour, so it clears within the hour.
Several providers have free tiers that are plenty for a small app.
